facts.statement: The study used two monkeys as the subjects.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Electrodes were placed in six specific brain areas involved in reaching and grasping.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Researchers stimulated five of the six implanted brain regions one at a time.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The method measured whether electrical pulses in one brain area caused immediate changes in the firing of neurons in other brain areas.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Stimulating any of the five active regions caused rapid, synchronized changes in most other recorded brain areas.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The effects were stronger and more frequent in the frontal lobe, especially in the primary motor cortex.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Computer programs trained to read brain signals could still work well even when the primary motor cortex was being stimulated nearby.
facts.subject: animals
